title: The Untold Story of Moses
paragraphs: There are stories in Scripture that people admire.
And then there are stories that quietly expose us.
The story of Moses was never just about plagues, miracles, parted seas, or stone tablets burning beneath the finger of God.
It is the terrifying, emotional, deeply human story of a man who spent most of his life feeling disqualified.
A man rescued by grace before he even knew the name of the God who rescued him.
A man who carried deliverance inside him while simultaneously battling insecurity, anger, fear, shame, loneliness, rejection, identity confusion, and emotional exhaustion.
Most people know the miracles of Moses.
Very few understand the wounds of Moses.
And maybe that is why this story still reaches deep into the human soul.
Because hidden beneath the surface of Exodus is the story of every believer who has ever asked:
“Can God still use someone like me?”
The untold story begins long before the burning bush.
The book of Exodus opens with Pharaoh terrified of the numerical growth of Israel. Exodus 1:22 says:
“Every son that is born you shall cast into the river.”
“Every born son into the Nile you must throw.”
This was demonic fear trying to kill a deliverer before he could grow.
Because God had already written a future hell could not erase.
His mother hides him for three months.
Then comes one of the most emotional scenes in all of Scripture.
A mother places her baby into a basket and releases him into the Nile.
The Hebrew word for basket in Exodus 2:3 is not the normal Hebrew word for basket.
The exact same word used for Noah’s ark.
Moses was placed into a miniature ark.
An instrument of salvation floating through judgment waters.
The Nile was supposed to become his grave.
Instead, it became the river carrying him toward destiny.
Some of you have been grieving the very waters God is using to move you.
The trauma did not destroy you.
The abandonment did not destroy you.
The betrayal did not destroy you.
The depression did not destroy you.
The wilderness did not destroy you.
You survived things that should have buried you.
And you still think your story is over.
Moses grows up inside Pharaoh’s palace.
Never fully accepted by either side.
“Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians.”
But none of it healed the identity war inside him.
Many people today know exactly what that feels like.
Looking successful publicly while privately feeling disconnected from who they really are.
And then comes the moment that changes everything.
Moses sees an Egyptian beating a Hebrew slave.
“He struck down the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.”
But he attempted to accomplish God’s purpose through human anger.
And many believers still do the same.
Trying to fulfill spiritual calling through fleshly reactions.
Trying to force destiny through emotional impulse.
Trying to heal wounds by controlling everything.
The next day, Moses discovers his secret is known.
And the prince of Egypt becomes a fugitive overnight.
And this is where most people stop paying attention.
Because the miracles have not started yet.
But the wilderness years may be the most important years of Moses’ entire life.
The same Moses who grew up in Pharaoh’s courts now lives in obscurity.
And maybe that is the part nobody wants to hear.
But God often develops people in silence.
God shapes souls in hidden valleys.
Moses spent decades thinking he failed.
Yet heaven was preparing him the entire time.
Somebody reading this has been frustrated because your life does not look how you imagined.
But hidden seasons are not wasted seasons.
God can do more in isolation than crowds can do in years.
“The angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush.”
God called Moses from the center of flames.
And what makes this moment unforgettable is this:
That is the story of every believer held together by grace.
In Hebrew culture, repeating a name carried intimacy, urgency, affection, and divine attention.
God was not calling a servant.
That word carries more than physical presence.
It is one of the most powerful responses in all of Scripture.
Most sermons skip how insecure Moses actually was.
“Who am I that I should go?”
“Heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue.”
Moses believed his weakness disqualified him.
Do you understand how revolutionary that is?
God did not deny Moses’ weakness.
Because calling was never dependent on Moses being enough.
It depended on God being enough.
This destroys the lie that perfection is required before obedience.
Some people are waiting until they feel fearless.
Some are waiting until they feel qualified.
And then comes the confrontation with Pharaoh.
The plagues were not random punishments.
They were direct judgments against Egyptian deities.
The Nile turning to blood confronted Hapi, the river god.
Darkness confronted Ra, the sun god.
The death of the firstborn confronted Pharaoh himself, who was considered divine.
God was dismantling false gods publicly.
Because every idol eventually collapses before the throne of the living God.
This was never merely Jewish history.
The Hebrew word for Passover is:
The blood became the difference between judgment and mercy.
And thousands of years later, Jesus Christ would become the final Passover Lamb.
“Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world.”
The Gospel was already whispering through Exodus.
And this is where the emotional tension becomes overwhelming.
And then God parts the sea.
But something people overlook is this:
The waters did not part until Moses moved forward.
Faith often requires movement before visible evidence.
And somebody reading this has been waiting for certainty before obedience.
But faith walks before it sees.
And finally, after centuries of slavery, freedom arrives.
Because freedom from Egypt did not instantly remove Egypt from their hearts.
That is one of the deepest spiritual realities in Exodus.
People can physically leave bondage while mentally remaining chained.
Which is why they constantly complained.
Constantly romanticized the slavery God rescued them from.
And if we are honest, many people still do the same.
Returning to patterns Christ died to free them from.
The mountain trembling beneath the glory of God.
But the Hebrew word for commandments is:
God was not merely giving rules.
The Law exposed humanity’s inability to save itself.
Which ultimately pointed toward the necessity of Jesus.
And then comes one of the saddest moments in Moses’ story.
While Moses is on the mountain with God, Israel creates the golden calf.
When people feel God is silent, they often create substitutes.
Even ministry can become an idol when it replaces intimacy with God.
The man who interceded for the people now watches them worship a false god.
Yet even after their rebellion, God still shows mercy.
Because mercy is the rhythm of Scripture.
And maybe somebody needed that reminder today.
You are not saved because your performance is flawless.
You are saved because Jesus is merciful.
But the untold story of Moses reaches its emotional climax near the end.
After decades of leading Israel through wilderness suffering, Moses makes one devastating mistake.
God tells him to speak to the rock.
“Hear now, you rebels: shall we bring water for you out of this rock?”
And Moses loses entrance into the Promised Land.
Yet even here, grace still appears.
Because Moses eventually stands in the Promised Land anyway.
And suddenly the deeper truth becomes visible.
Moses was never the final deliverer.
Moses brought commandments written on stone.
Jesus writes transformation onto human hearts.
Jesus intercedes eternally for all who believe.
The entire story of Moses ultimately points to Christ.
And maybe that is why this story still wrecks people emotionally.
And Jesus reflects the Savior humanity desperately needs.
The untold story of Moses is not really about a superhero.
It is about what God can do with surrendered weakness.
And maybe you have spent years believing your failures ruined your purpose.
Maybe shame convinced you God moved on from you.
Maybe your hidden battles feel too ugly.
Maybe your past feels louder than your future.
But Moses is proof that God still calls wounded people.
Still writes miracles through trembling hands.
And maybe this article exposed something you have been hiding for a long time.
Because Scripture is not merely history.
Send this to someone who feels disqualified.
The same God who preserved Moses in the river is still preserving people who feel like they are drowning.
Ang Hindi Naikukuwentong Kuwento ni Moises
May mga kuwento sa Bibliya na hinahangaan ng tao.
At may mga kuwento namang tahimik na binabasag ang puso ng tao.
Ang kuwento ni Moises ay hindi lang kuwento tungkol sa sampung salot, paghahati ng Dagat na Pula, o mga tapyas ng bato na isinulat ng daliri ng Diyos.
Ito ay kuwento ng isang lalaking halos buong buhay ay pakiramdam niya hindi siya sapat.
Isang lalaking iniligtas ng biyaya bago pa niya lubos na makilala ang Diyos na nagligtas sa kanya.
Isang lalaking may dalang pagtawag ng Diyos pero punong-puno ng takot, galit, pagod, pagdududa, trauma, at mga sugat na walang nakakakita.
Kilala ng karamihan ang mga himala ni Moises.
Pero kakaunti ang tunay na nakakaunawa sa mga sugat ni Moises.
At baka iyon ang dahilan kung bakit hanggang ngayon tumatagos pa rin ito sa kaluluwa ng tao.
Dahil sa ilalim ng aklat ng Exodo ay nakatago ang kuwento ng bawat taong minsang nagtanong:
“Magagamit pa ba ako ng Diyos kahit ganito ako?”
Nagsimula ang kuwento hindi sa nagliliyab na puno.
“Bawat lalaking sanggol na ipanganak ay ihagis sa ilog.”
“Bawat batang lalaking ipinanganak ay ihagis sa Nile.”
Takot ng kadiliman sa isang batang magiging tagapagligtas balang araw.
At kahit gustong patayin ng mundo si Moises… nabuhay pa rin siya.
Kundi dahil may isinulat nang plano ang Diyos na hindi kayang burahin ng impiyerno.
Itinago siya ng kanyang ina nang tatlong buwan.
At dumating ang isa sa pinakamabigat na tagpo sa buong Kasulatan.
Isang ina ang naglagay ng kanyang sanggol sa basket at pinaanod sa ilog.
Ang nakakagulat… ang salitang ginamit sa Hebrew para sa basket ay:
Ito rin mismo ang salitang ginamit para sa arka ni Noe.
Si Moises ay inilagay sa isang maliit na “arka.”
Isang sisidlan ng pagliligtas sa gitna ng tubig ng kamatayan.
Ang Nile sana ang magiging libingan niya.
Pero ginawa iyon ng Diyos na daan patungo sa kanyang destinasyon.
May mga taong nagbabasa nito ngayon na akala nila tapos na ang buhay nila.
Akala mo winasak ka ng trauma.
Akala mo tinapos ka ng depresyon.
Akala mo walang saysay ang pag-iyak mo gabi-gabi.
At baka hindi mo pa alam… pero may dahilan kung bakit hindi ka pinabayaan ng Diyos.
Lumaki si Moises sa palasyo ni Paraon.
Lumaking hindi lubos na tanggap saanman.
“Tinuruan si Moises ng lahat ng karunungan ng mga Egipcio.”
Pero walang nakapagpagaling sa digmaan sa loob niya.
At dumating ang araw na nagbago ang lahat.
Nakita ni Moises ang isang Egipcio na sinasaktan ang isang Hebreo.
Pero sinubukan niyang gawin ang plano ng Diyos gamit ang laman.
At hanggang ngayon, maraming tao pa rin ang gumagawa niyan.
Pinipilit ang calling gamit ang emosyon.
Pinapairal ang galit sa halip na pagsunod.
Kinokontrol ang lahat dahil takot masaktan muli.
Nang malaman ni Paraon ang nangyari, tumakas si Moises.
Ang prinsipe ng Egypt naging takas.
At dito nagsimula ang bahagi ng kuwento na madalas hindi pinapansin.
Ang dating nakatira sa palasyo… ngayon nasa disyerto.
At baka ito ang ayaw marinig ng modernong mundo.
Pero madalas humuhubog ang Diyos sa katahimikan.
Pero ang Diyos gumagawa muna ng shepherd.
Pero ang Diyos naghahanda sa lihim.
Akala ni Moises tapos na ang buhay niya.
Hindi niya alam… inihahanda na pala siya ng langit.
May taong nagbabasa nito na frustrado dahil parang walang nangyayari sa buhay mo.
Pero ang mga nakatagong season ay hindi sayang.
May ginagawa ang Diyos kahit hindi mo nakikita.
At dumating ang nagliliyab na puno.
“Nagpakita ang anghel ng Panginoon sa apoy sa gitna ng isang mababang punongkahoy.”
Tinawag ng Diyos si Moises mula sa gitna ng apoy.
Iyan ang larawan ng maraming mananampalataya ngayon.
Pero hindi pa rin tuluyang bumabagsak.
Mahalaga ang pag-uulit ng pangalan sa kultura ng Hebrew.
Hindi lang tinatawag ng Diyos ang isang lingkod.
At pagkatapos nito… nakipagtalo si Moises sa Diyos.
Madalas hindi ito pinapansin sa mga sermon.
Pakiramdam ni Moises hindi siya sapat.
Pero pinili pa rin siya ng Diyos.
At iyan ang bumabasag sa kasinungalingan ng maraming tao.
Hindi hinihintay ng Diyos na maging perpekto ka.
Maraming tao naghihintay maging fearless bago sumunod.
Pero ang Diyos humahanap ng willing.
At nagsimula ang laban kay Paraon.
Ang sampung salot ay hindi random.
Bawat isa ay pagwasak ng Diyos sa mga diyos-diyosan ng Egypt.
Ang kamatayan ng panganay laban kay Paraon na itinuturing na diyos.
Walang diyos-diyosan ang makakatayo sa harapan Niya.
At hanggang ngayon ganoon pa rin.
Hindi kayang iligtas ng pera ang kaluluwa.
Hindi kayang pagalingin ng fame ang emptiness.
Hindi kayang punuin ng kasalanan ang espiritu.
Ang dugo ang naging pagitan ng awa at paghatol.
At pagdating ni Jesus… nakita ng mundo ang tunay na Kordero ng Diyos.
“Masdan ang Kordero ng Diyos na nag-aalis ng kasalanan ng sanlibutan.”
Mula pa noon… ibinubulong na ng Exodus ang tungkol kay Cristo.
Pagdating sa Dagat na Pula, natakot ang Israel.
Nasa likod nila ang hukbo ni Paraon.
At saka hinati ng Diyos ang dagat.
Pero may bagay na madalas hindi napapansin.
Hindi nahati ang tubig hanggang hindi gumalaw si Moises.
Minsan hinihintay natin ang malinaw na ebidensya bago sumunod.
Pero ang tunay na pananampalataya kumikilos muna.
At nang makatawid sila… akala nila tapos na ang laban.
Dahil kahit nakalabas na sila sa Egypt… nasa puso pa rin nila ang Egypt.
At hanggang ngayon maraming tao ang ganyan.
Pero bumabalik pa rin sa kasalanan.
Pagdating sa Sinai, ibinigay ng Diyos ang kautusan.
Pero ang salitang ginamit sa Hebrew para sa commandments ay:
Hindi lang nagbibigay ng rules ang Diyos.
At habang nasa bundok si Moises… gumawa naman ng gintong guya ang Israel.
At ang impatience madalas nagbubunga ng idolatry.
Kapag pakiramdam ng tao tahimik ang Diyos… gumagawa siya ng substitute.
At kahit nagkasala ang Israel… nagpakita pa rin ng awa ang Diyos.
At baka kailangan marinig ito ng isang tao ngayon.
Hindi ka naligtas dahil flawless ka.
Naligtas ka dahil maawain si Jesus.
At dumating ang pinakamasakit na bahagi ng kuwento.
Sinabihan ng Diyos si Moises na kausapin ang bato.
At dahil dito… hindi siya nakapasok sa Promised Land.
Pero kahit dito… may biyaya pa rin.
Dahil kalaunan nakita rin si Moises sa Promised Land.
Kundi sa Mount of Transfiguration kasama ni Jesus.
At doon naging malinaw ang mas malalim na katotohanan.
Si Moises ay hindi ang tunay na tagapagligtas.
Inilabas ni Moises ang Israel mula Egypt.
Pero inililigtas ni Jesus ang tao mula sa kasalanan.
Pero tinalo ni Jesus ang kamatayan.
Nagbigay si Moises ng kautusan sa bato.
Pero si Jesus nagsusulat ng pagbabago sa puso.
Ang buong kuwento ni Moises ay tumuturo kay Cristo.
At baka kaya ito sobrang tumatama sa tao.
Dahil nakikita natin ang sarili natin kay Moises.
Pero patuloy pa ring tinatawag ng Diyos.
At baka pakiramdam mo wala nang pag-asa para sa’yo.
Baka akala mo tapos na ang purpose mo.
Baka pakiramdam mo hindi ka na kayang gamitin ng Diyos.
Ginagamit pa rin ng Diyos ang mga sugatan.
Tinatawag pa rin Niya ang mga insecure.
Pinapatawad pa rin Niya ang mga bagsak.
At gumagawa pa rin Siya ng himala gamit ang nanginginig na kamay.
Mas malalim ito kaysa simpleng impormasyon.
Dahil ang Biblia ay hindi lang history.
Ang parehong Diyos na nagligtas kay Moises sa ilog ay Siya ring Diyos na patuloy na nagliligtas sa mga taong pakiramdam nila nalulunod na sila.
